$comment: G7 canary fixtures (plan §6). Release-facing claims captured from the trees that falsified them, quoted verbatim (row 9 is the one condensation, flagged in its own `origin`). THREE capture waves, declared in `captureWaves` and named per row by `wave` — there is no single fixture-wide commit: rows 1-2 are pre-framework-slim, rows 3-9 are the pre-single-entry `root-full` family, and rows 10-20 are what the convergence commit itself left behind (rows 10-11, 16 and 17-20 pre-date it and were falsified by it; rows 12-15 its token-level rewrite minted). Rows 17-20 were captured by the exhaustive-closure round: 17 proves the modal `root entry … is absent` wording, and 18-20 the three costumes of the same claim that never say the word `root` — the dist file name, `the core entry out`, and a bare `without either`. With them EVERY alternative of the `root-free` family is proved against the exact sentence it exists to kill. The G7 gate FAILS unless its pattern set matches ALL of them, which is what proves the patterns work against the exact claims they exist to kill; it also fails if a row's `wave` does not resolve, because a canary that cannot say where it came from sends the next reader to the wrong tree. This file is NOT part of the G7 corpus (scripts/ is out of scope), so it cannot self-collide. Never edit the text: it is a historical snapshot, not documentation.

The tree the single-entry convergence cut: @comvi/core was still the batteries-included composed root and @comvi/core/slim was the separate base host.

The convergence commit itself, read before the prose repair: what its token-level rewrite left behind — claims it minted, and pre-convergence claims it carried through unchanged and thereby falsified.
